extracted.intended_audience: media outlets, businesses, event organisers, fans and third parties seeking guidance on use of FIFA World Cup 26™ intellectual property
extracted.subtask_short: FIFA World Cup IP usage guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Official FIFA guidance on what constitutes authorised vs. unauthorised use of FIFA World Cup 26™ intellectual property across media, commercial, retail, public viewing and on-site contexts, and how third parties can engage without creating an unauthorised commercial association.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA ownership of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA holds all rights in relation to the FIFA World Cup 26™, which include all intellectual property, media, marketing, licensing, ticketing and other commercial rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rights enable FIFA to control commercial exploitation of the Tournament and to grant exclusivity to Rights Holders. The document makes clear that FIFA enforces and protects those rights globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Official Intellectual Property
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA has developed a range of brand assets, including logos, words, titles, symbols and other identifiers in connection with the Tournament and FIFA ('Official Intellectual Property').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include the Official Emblem, Official Wordmark, Official Slogan(s), Host City Logos and Slogans, Official Mascot, Official Poster, Official Trophy, FIFA Corporate Mark, FIFA Plus Mark, listed word marks (e.g., 'FIFA World Cup 26™', 'World Cup™', 'FIFA®', etc.), and the Official Typeface 'FWC 2026'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal protection of Official Intellectual Property
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Intellectual Property is protected in the United States, Canada and Mexico and territories around the world by copyright, trademark and/or other forms of intellectual property and laws such as unfair competition, passing off and any other relevant laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These laws protect FIFA against the unauthorised use of identical reproductions and confusingly similar variations and modifications of the Official Intellectual Property. For a comprehensive overview in a specific country, consult local IP offices or professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial use restricted to FIFA Rights Holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Only FIFA Rights Holders are permitted to use the Official Intellectual Property for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not a FIFA Rights Holder and would like to request the use of the Official Emblem or other official marks for editorial purposes, visit www.fifadigitalarchive.com. Commercial use by non-Rights Holders will be subject to enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of FIFA Rights Holders and their entitlements
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA Rights Holders include tiers of Commercial Affiliates (FIFA Partners, FIFA World Cup Sponsor Plus, FIFA World Cup Sponsors, FIFA World Cup Tournament Supporters), Host Committee/Host City Supporters/Host City Donors, Media Rights Licensees, Branded/Unbranded Licensees, Official Suppliers and an appointed Hospitality rights holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category receives defined commercial/media/licensing rights (e.g., TV, radio, broadband, IPTV, mobile for Media Rights Licensees; rights to manufacture official licensed products for Branded Licensees). Further details available on FIFA's commercial pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on creating an unauthorised commercial association
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities that create an undue commercial association are not permitted and are subject to legal measures. Such undue commercial association is established when a company makes it appear as if it is associated with FIFA or the Tournament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid infringement, FIFA encourages use of generic football or country-related imagery/terminology and suggests seeking independent legal advice. The guidelines are not a defence for deliberate ambush marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial use by media: permitted but limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Any legitimate editorial use, such as content specifically reporting on the Tournament, does not create an unauthorised association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, Official Intellectual Property cannot be used as an integral part of a publication's layout, as elements of the brand of a publication, or on a stand-alone/recurring/static basis on a website (e.g., repeated corner logos or every page of a special subsection), as that may suggest FIFA endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media mark requests and graphic guideline compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Media outlets may request digital copies of the Official Intellectual Property free of charge via https://www.fifadigitalarchive.com/welcome/markrequest/.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested artwork must be used in compliance with FIFA’s graphic guidelines, which are provided along with the high-quality digital files. Use is limited to editorial purposes that do not create undue association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media — fan vs commercial usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of Official Intellectual Property by fans, without commercial intent, is generally accepted, and hashtags and retweets by fans without commercial benefit are generally accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive use by fans may create the impression of association and should be avoided. Retweeting or sharing official content for commercial purposes is an exclusive right of FIFA Rights Holders. The use of Official Intellectual Property in hashtags by company profiles with commercial benefit is restricted to FIFA and Rights Holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use in social media by third parties with commercial benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Retweeting or sharing official content for commercial purposes and the use of Official Intellectual Property in hashtags by (company) profiles with commercial benefits creates a commercial association and is restricted to FIFA and FIFA Rights Holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial social profiles should avoid Official IP unless authorised; doing otherwise risks enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile and internet services/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of Official Intellectual Property or broadcast content for commercial purposes in applications and/or any other mobile/internet services is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/descriptive use is permissible provided there is no risk of confusion that the service is connected with FIFA or the Tournament. Names or titles may not incorporate Official Intellectual Property in a manner suggesting endorsement (e.g., full event title or Official Emblem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain names, URLs and hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Intellectual Property may not be incorporated in domain names, unless authorised by FIFA. The use of Official Intellectual Property in URLs or hyperlinks by commercial websites is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial sites should avoid embedding FIFA marks in domain names or link text that could suggest an affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Websites: 'look and feel' restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Intellectual Property may not be used as part of the overall design of a website or webpage (including background or wallpaper designs) if it is likely to create the impression of an association with the Tournament/FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using Official IP in site templates, headers, footers or repeated design elements that imply endorsement or sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial blogs and non-commercial commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Intellectual Property used on editorial blogs, reporting or commenting on the Tournament without any commercial content or advertising generally does not create an unauthorised association and is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a blog includes commercial content or advertising, the use may then create an unauthorised association and should be avoided unless authorised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business advertisements and promotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Using any Official Intellectual Property in commercial advertisements is likely to create an unauthorised association and is therefore to be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial adverts should not display Official IP nor place such marks in proximity to company logos or references like 'Brought to you by...','Presented by...', or 'Sponsored by...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitions, games and lotteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitions, games or lotteries using any Official Intellectual Property or creating a commercial association with the Tournament, unless authorised by FIFA, are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes prize draws, incentives, online auctions and similar consumer promotions unless organised/authorised by FIFA or a Rights Holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticket promotions and unauthorised ticket sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless authorised by FIFA or organised in cooperation with a FIFA Rights Holder, it is not permitted to use Tickets for the Tournament for promotional purposes, prize draws, incentives, online auctions and/or any other type of consumer promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tickets obtained through unauthorised ticket promotions will be cancelled once identified and access to the stadium will therefore not be granted. Report suspected unauthorised sales to ticketenforcement@fifa.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match schedule use
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial, non-commercial use or reproduction of the official FIFA match schedule does not create an unauthorised association and is generally accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial use of the match schedule together with or in proximity to a company logo or commercial reference (e.g., 'Presented by...') is not permitted. The match schedule is protected by copyright and other IP rights in many countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Countdown clocks and tickers
rubrics_metrics.description: Any commercially branded tool created to count down to the Tournament creates an unauthorised association, whether physical or online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countdowns used for commercial promotion should avoid branding that ties them to FIFA/Tournament marks unless authorised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business names and branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Intellectual Property used as part of any business name, in any context, without the authorisation of FIFA is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Businesses should not register or trade under names incorporating FIFA/World Cup marks; seek licensing/cooperation with a Rights Holder if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-store decorations
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic football or country-related in-store decorations do not create an unauthorised association and are generally accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Intellectual Property is not permitted for use as in-store decorations unless authorised by FIFA or via a FIFA Rights Holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merchandise and licensed products
rubrics_metrics.description: Items with generic football terms and/or country names or national flags do not create an infringement of FIFA’s rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of Official Intellectual Property or any element thereof on merchandising items is an exclusive right of FIFA Rights Holders and is therefore not permitted for unauthorised third parties. Contact retail-licensing@fifa.org for licensing opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public viewing and exhibitor licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorised public viewing exhibitors must comply with the FIFA World Cup 26™ Regulations for Public Viewing Events and obtain a licence granted by FIFA or its Media Rights Licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other public displays showing moving images from the matches should avoid using Official Intellectual Property or advertising sponsorship that may create an unauthorised association. Public viewing regulations and licence details will be available on FIFA.com closer to the Tournament.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site restrictions (hospitality, distribution of branded items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of fans, including hospitality guest groups, may not display or wear items with the same prominent non-FIFA branding, including signs guiding groups to the stadium, which create an unauthorised association and violate the Ticketing Terms and Conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution of branded items on matchdays in the area surrounding the stadium without necessary approval is not permitted as it creates an unauthorised association. This includes branded clothing, flags or other items that suggest sponsorship/endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of the Guidelines (non-exhaustive; not a legal determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: These guidelines provide information and guidance to interested parties on FIFA’s intellectual property and other commercial rights... The examples provided herein are non-exhaustive. These guidelines explicitly do not confirm whether or not an activity infringes any rights in relation to the FIFA World Cup 26™.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA cannot provide guidance on every potential activity; the guidelines are for general information only and parties should seek independent legal advice where necessary. All rights explicitly reserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact points, licensing and enforcement processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information and channels to get involved or report issues (sponsorship: sales@fifa.org; licensing: retail-licensing@fifa.org; public viewing: https://publicviewing.fifa.org/public_viewing; mark requests: fifadigitalarchive mark request form; unauthorised ticket sales: ticketenforcement@fifa.org; unauthorised IP use: brandprotection@fifa.org).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document identifies routes for requesting editorial marks, applying for licences, reporting unauthorised promotions or IP infringements, and for rights-holders/sponsors to engage with FIFA.
